bank_access: Effectively blocked remotely: banks (BCC-supervised) require in-person branch visit, local tax ID (NIF) and local address; no remote onboarding for non-resident entities.
Needs a local visit: CFA-CEMAC banks (BGFI, BICEC, SGB) require in-person KYC with passport, residence permit and local address; remote opening not available for foreign entities.
Needs a local visit: BANGE/BGFIBank branches require in-person appearance with passport/residence card and local address; no remote onboarding for non-residents; rules not fully verified.
Personal accounts can be opened remotely by intermediaries, but an NGO corporate account in practice needs in-person KYC in the capital with local address and NIF tax number.
Needs a local visit: banks (Bank of Kigali, I&M, KCB) require physical attendance for in-person interview under AML Law 75/2019; non-resident business accounts need a trip to Kigali.
Needs a local visit: banks in Bujumbura (BCB, BCB) require in-person appearance with passport and proof of residence; standard AML/CFT checks, no remote opening for foreign entities.
In-person at major banks (Stanbic, Absa, DFCU): passport, URA TIN, board resolution and named signatories; no local address required for foreign-registered entities, no remote opening.
Needs a local visit: banks (CRDB, NMB, Stanbic) require in-person application with passport, TIN and proof of residence; foreign NGOs register at national level; no remote onboarding.
In-person at branch under CBK AML/KYC rules; NGO accounts require at least one Kenyan-resident board member as signatory plus an NGO Board recommendation letter, so a local representative is needed.
Needs a local visit: opening an account in Moroni requires in-person appearance with passport, residence permit and local address; offshore non-resident accounts do not suit charity banking.
Needs a local visit: banks (BOA, BMOI, MCB) require in-person appearance with passport, residence permit, local address proof and NIF tax ID; minimum deposit, no remote opening.
In-person at branch: ZRA TPIN mandatory, local address proof (<3 months) and in-person signature collection; foreign NGOs need resident directors/signatories per bank CDD.
Needs a local visit: banks in Lilongwe/Blantyre (StandChart, Centenary, FCB) require in-person appearance with passport, TIN and local address proof; no remote onboarding for foreign entities.
Non-residents may open accounts with NUIT tax ID, but in-person branch visit is required (BCI, Millennium BIM, FNB); foreign-authorized NGOs need local address and resident signatories.
In-person only (no online option): NIF tax ID is the usual bottleneck, plus passport with valid visa/resident card at a branch; banks cannot onboard foreign entities remotely.
Needs a local visit: banks (StandChart, FNB, Stanbic) typically require a residence permit and in-person appearance with local address; remote onboarding not available for foreign entities.
In-person is typical (Bank Windhoek opens permanent accounts even without residence status); some banks (Nedbank) allow remote opening via power of attorney, so a local agent can arrange it.
In-person KYC at branch (RBZ-supervised AML) with passport and address proof; diaspora products exist for individuals, but charity/NGO accounts need in-person signing with local signatories.
Needs a local visit: non-resident accounts at Standard Bank/FNB/Nedbank require in-person appearance in Mbabane with passport and proof of address; no remote onboarding.
Needs a local visit: banks (PostBank, Stanbic, Nedbank) require in-person verification with passport, residence permit and local proof of residence; no remote onboarding for foreign entities.
